subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Instant Coffee: Accident or Invention?
description: One-minute skill: Instant Coffee: Accident or Invention?.

hook.text: Instant coffee was first mass-produced in 1910 by George Washington—not the president, but a Belgian-American inventor.

buildup.text: Washington noticed dried coffee residue on his carafe lid. He realized brewed coffee could be dehydrated and reconstituted.

discovery.text: His Red E Coffee launched in 1910. During WWI, soldiers loved it—they called any instant coffee 'a cup of George.'

twist.text: Nestlé's Nescafé (1938) perfected the formula. Brazil's coffee surplus funded the research—too many beans to sell.

climax.text: Today, instant coffee outsells brewed in most of the world. Only in the US and parts of Europe does fresh brewing dominate.

punchline.text: Dried residue on a lid, a wartime staple, a global default. Accidents scale.

quiz.question: What inspired George Washington to create instant coffee?
options: He noticed dried coffee residue on his silver carafe lid could be reconstituted
